Journal.Title: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology

Article.ArticleTitle: Heightened Cortisol Response to Exercise Challenge in Women with Functional Hypothalamic Amenorrhea.

Abstract.AbstractText: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea is characterized by anovulation due to reduced gonadotropin-releasing hormone drive and is associated with hypercortisolemia that has been linked to heightened hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal reactivity to common psychological and metabolic challenges.
We hypothesized that women with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea would display greater cortisol responses to exercise challenge than ovulatory, eumenorrheic women.

Cross-sectional comparison of 9 women with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea and 11 eumenorrheic women who were of reproductive age, weighed 90-110% ideal body weight, did not exercise excessively, and had no formal psychiatric diagnosis. Subjects completed a 20-min submaximal exercise challenge using a cycle ergometer in a research exercise lab. Heart rate and circulatory cortisol, glucose, and lactate were measured at 10-minute intervals before, during, and after the exercise challenge.

Baseline (t = -10 min) cortisol, glucose, lactate, and heart rate were comparable between groups. Glucose levels rose modestly during exercise by 2.9% in eumenorrheic women, p=0.4, but declined by 10.6% in functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, p<0.03. The nadir in glucose levels in functional hypothalamic amenorrhea occurred at the end of the 20-min exercise challenge (t = +20 min). Lactate levels rose comparably in both groups, p<0.01. Heart rate increased significantly with exercise in both groups, p<0.01, but the increase was smaller in subjects with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, p<0.01. Cortisol increased during the exercise challenge in both groups, p<0.01, and peaked 10 min after the exercise ended (t = +30 min). At peak, subjects with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea displayed higher cortisol levels (147 ± 22 (SEM) ng/mL) than eumenorrheic women (96 ± 12 ng/mL), p=0.05. The mean percent increase over baseline was 62% in eumenorrheic women and 92% in functional hypothalamic amenorrhea.

The heightened cortisol response to exercise in women with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea was associated with a decline in blood glucose that was not observed in eumenorrheic women. Women with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea appear to be more reactive at the endocrine level to the metabolic demand of exercise. Submaximal challenge unmasks underlying stress sensitivity in women with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea and highlights the importance of using psychological interventions for stress reduction in this population.
